FIXED by re-expressing the assertion. NO product change — and that mattered here more than usual, because satisfying the check as written would have required GRANTING SuperUser the license-issuer permissions, i.e. removing a security boundary to make a test green. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE at three layers, not from memory: (1) Permissions.ts builds SUPER_USER_PERMISSIONS as ALL_PERMISSIONS minus ISSUER_PERMISSIONS with the documented reason 'so a direct grant or the Super Users broad permission set can never become a signing-key boundary bypass'; (2) the Issuer built-in role holds exactly those two; (3) UserAdminService rejects an Issuer who also holds any other role (ISSUER_ROLE_EXCLUSIVE) and the licenseIssuer route requires that exact role. CORRECTION TO THIS BEADS OWN INSTRUCTION: it proposed asserting the issuer set is held by NO built-in role. That would have been wrong — the Issuer role holds them by design. Checked before writing, so it did not ship. THE SANITY INTENT IS KEPT, NOT DROPPED. One assertion became three: SuperUser holds every permission except the issuer pair; the ONLY permissions withheld from SuperUser are that pair (an exact set difference, so a newly withheld permission still fails); and the Issuer role holds exactly that pair, so neither permission is orphaned nor bundled with unrelated power. The two names are restated in the verifier rather than imported (ISSUER_PERMISSIONS is not exported), so widening the boundary in the product surfaces as a failure needing review instead of being mirrored silently. MUTATION-TESTED, 3 mutations, each caught by its intended check: M1 grant SuperUser the issuer permissions — the exact change the OLD assertion demanded — now FAILS the boundary check (48/49); M2 widen ISSUER_PERMISSIONS to withhold a third permission fails all three (46/49); M3 empty the Issuer role fails only the orphan check (48/49). So the verifier has flipped from requiring a security regression to forbidding one.
